Method of Attack: PowerExchange: PowerShell backdoor accepting commands via Microsoft Exchange, executing arbitrary PowerShell commands, exfiltrating data, and hiding traces by moving emails to 'Deleted Items'.
Backdoor.Tokel: Executes PowerShell commands and downloads files.
Trojan.Dirps: Enumerates files and runs PowerShell commands.
Infostealer.Clipog: Steals clipboard data and captures keystrokes.
Plink: Command-line tool for PuTTY SSH client used for RDP access and SSH tunnels.
Backdoor.Token: Implant executed on breached machines.
TrojanDirps: Enumerates files and runs PowerShell commands.
Impacted Systems: Government organization systems in the United Arab Emirates
At least 12 computers on victim's network
Dozens more systems with backdoors and keyloggers
Attack Vector: Compromise via PowerShell scripts and commands
Masqueraded Plink executable ('mssh.exe') for RDP configuration
Use of Microsoft Exchange for command and control
Use of certutil to download tools
Date of Discovery: February to September 2023 (attack period observed by Symantec)
